## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sukkātherīgāthā* (Thig 3.6) is a short poem in the *Therīgāthā* attributed to the enlightened nun (*bhikkhunī*) Sukkā, consisting of verses numbered 54–56 in the collection [SuttaCentral; Collett 2014; Sujato 2009]. In comparative vinaya literature, verses 6–7 of the Lokuttaravāda Vinaya (concerning a nun styled Śuklā Karmāradhītā) are noted to be strikingly similar to the verses of Sukkā found at Therīgāthā 54 and 55 [Sujato 2009]. Modern English translations of the text include those by Ayya Soma and Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Sukkā is celebrated elsewhere across early Buddhist literature, most notably in the *Samyutta Nikāya* [Collett 2014]. SuttaCentral records a direct parallel to these verses in the *Paṭhamasukkāsutta* (SN 10.9) of the *Yakkha Saṁyutta*, where an inspired *yakkha* wanders through the streets and crossroads of Rājagaha proclaiming Sukkā's teaching and urging the citizens to honor and support her [SuttaCentral; Rhys Davids 1917; Hazra 1994]. Sukkā's life and verses are further expanded in the *Apadāna* (*Sukkātherīapadāna*, Thi-Ap 35) [SuttaCentral; Rhys Davids 1917].

Text-reuse analysis by DharmaNexus registers four internal matches with the *Therīgāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, where the commentary embeds the verses (§§1.1–2.2 aligning with commentary §§848–851) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also generates four automatic cross-language alignments with the Tibetan translation of the *ārya-saddharmānusmṛtyupasthāna* (D0287-2), though at a very low plausibility score (score 10) not recognized as a true textual parallel by SuttaCentral [DharmaNexus].
